title: Credible sets
bodyHtml:
Credible sets are sets of variants near a genetic association signal that are predicted, with a specific probability, to include the causal variant for that signal. These sets are generated by fine mapping, an additional step that is often applied to GWAS results to investigate in detail the region around a variant that is significantly associated with a phenotype. Several different methods are commonly used for fine mapping.

Currently available credible sets are listed in the table below. We aim to incorporate credible sets and their accompanying GWAS results for as many traits as possible. If you have generated credible sets that are not currently displayed in the Portals, please contact us to contribute them.

Credible set membership of variants may be viewed in the Variant Sifter tool.

Click on a column header to sort the table by that column. Filter the table using the filters above:

  • enter a full or partial dataset name into the Dataset filter and select a name
  • enter a full or partial phenotype name into the Phenotype filter and select a phenotype
  • enter the full or partial name of a phenotype group into the Phenotype group filter and select a group to see credible sets for phenotypes in that group
  • filter by Ancestry or Method by choosing from the pull-down menus
  • begin typing an author name, publication title, or journal name into the Reference filter and select a publication

Multiple filters may be combined.

Click on a dataset name in the Accompanying GWAS column to navigate to the Dataset page for the GWAS on which the credible set is based.
